speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) (a) what are the criteria to qualify a company to conduct Workforce Skills Qualifications courses; (b) what can students do when the quality of the instructors is not as advertised; and (c) how does the Ministry oversee these companies to ensure they are not overcharging.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: So, even after they are appointed, we will continue to do random audits to ensure that they comply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: If not, upon renewal, it may be revoked.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: Course participants can directly provide feedback and views on the quality of learning on the respective SkillsFuture Credit-eligible courses they attended.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: I also would like to share with the Members that this year, SSG will publish on MySkillsFuture portal, information on the training outcomes of SSG-supported courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: So, you can see more information about the courses to make an informed decision.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: This is done because we want to make available information for individuals or Singaporeans to make more informed learning choices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: It will also serve to heighten the ATOs' accountability for results in their training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: SSG will continue to look for ways of improving greater transparency and information on training quality and impact.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: But we all know in a free market, the best safeguard against unreasonable pricing is competition.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: Today, we have about 500 training providers delivering WSQ courses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Learning and Skills))
text: In a way, it serves as some form of check on the course fees.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Ms Chia Yong Yong, you have a supplementary question?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: I have a question for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: In any application for accreditation by a potential service provider or trainers, are the applicants required to declare any association or relations to other service providers who may have been under investigation or who may have been penalised for any improper conduct?

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: And such association might include relationships to shareholders, directors and managers of errant or suspected errant trainers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Nominated Member of Parliament Ms Chia Yong Yong for her supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I highlighted the six-pronged criteria that SSG will take into consideration when they evaluate, as to whether we should appoint the ATO.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will certainly also look at the track record of the organisation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is where I also want to reassure her and Members if any members of the public are aware that a particular organisation, in terms of the history or background, is quite dubious, because of their linkages with other service providers, we welcome them to step forward and share this information with SSG.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: On Monday, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about the number for the hotline.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Operating hours are from Monday to Friday, 8.30 am to 5.30 pm, and on Saturday, 8.30 am to 1.00 pm.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For any other hours outside of the operating hours, please assure your residents or members of the public to leave their contact details.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will close the loop with them during the next working day.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition, if the members of the public prefer to send in their feedback via email or even via the MySkillsFuture portal, they can do so through the new feature I mentioned earlier – community feedback feature.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: That is why I think a lot of people jump into this.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: How can the Ministry provide more information to course applicants to make an informed decision?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The second question is, will the Ministry consider open review of courses?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Just like when we want to book hotels or restaurants overseas, there are always some reviews for us to view.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, will the Ministry consider that, so that when a participant wants to go for that course, they will look at the reviews?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want thank Er Dr Lee Bee Wah for her supplementary questions and I want to assure her and the Members in the House that the Ministry of Education (MOE) has stringent standards on the quality of the WSQ training providers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we want to ensure the competency of the training providers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This covers areas such as effective learning, standards of the trainers, course content, the ability to apply the learning, impact on job performance and job scope, as well as the providers' customer service.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we want to assure Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Members that course applicants can be assured that the key criteria of quality, course transparency and accountability really underpin SSG's efforts to enhance Singaporeans' learning needs.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Ministry consider ranking these training providers based on the quality of teaching?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Very often, we hear of the main trainers to be ACTA accredited but then, if they are not there, the relief trainers do not have that certification.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Ms Thanaletchimi for her suggestions which we will consider.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In practical terms, what could be a top training organisation may not exactly be a top one for another course applicant; it depends on their learning needs, what industry they are in, and so on.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to elaborate because I think Ms Thanaletchimi will be quite keen.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, all hands on deck, we are trying to level up the professional standards of the adult educators to ensure that Singaporeans who want to level up their education, their skills, will be well placed to do so.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Just now, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned about feedback by course participants.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Also, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary did not reply to my specific question of an open review system.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: If it is an open review, people can easily go online to see the reviews of past participants.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Er Dr Lee Bee Wah for her question.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: With regards to feedback, it will be collected using a two-prong approach.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Many of us would have attended courses and at the end of the course, you probably would be given a feedback form.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Indeed, there may be some course participants' views which may be moderated.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: This is why we have recently introduced a new feature on the MySkillsFuture portal.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For residents who feel more comfortable calling, I have provided the hotline.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: There are many ways to get to us to make sure that Singaporeans have all channels to provide us information of any ATO or training provider, if they suspect any malpractice or any misleading marketing practices or even fraudulent activities.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I thought I had answered that question but let me do that again.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The Member talked about open review and I highlighted that starting this month we will progressively put out more information on the portal and those information cannot just come from nowhere.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: The information in areas that I mentioned, for example trainees rating, must come from the participants of the courses previously.
